case: A genuine candidate-era name -- held by neither registry -- added to the table, mapping to a real record.
why: The table must stay ADDABLE. It exists because four of the five F2 candidates proposed renaming existing records, and the whole point is that a candidate-era name resolves here for reading instead of being admitted as a record name. A check that refused new rows would make publishing a correspondence more expensive than leaving a reader to guess, which inverts what the file is for. The widened refusal must key on `this name is one the package HAS`, not on `this row is new`.
